{"base_state_digest":"8afd8a09bf216d3c8abe4ca64bf15a212ae5022bb0234699eb8e00465003811f","certificate_id":"c9e4b1bd76b3961204404c4419d6685de4793517389976ed36abdfcb5df6073a","target":{"node_id":"n3","version":2},"operation":"replace","nodes":[{"node_id":"n3","text":"If \(n=1\), no block can be removed, so \(b(1)=0\), and hence \(14b(1)=0\ge -2=2(1)^2-4(1)\). Now suppose \(n\ge2\). By the potential-triple count, there are \(T=2n(n-2)\) potential triples, and every one is hit in the final blocked configuration. Since each removed block hits at most \(14\) potential triples, counting incidences gives
\[
14\,b(n)\ge T=2n(n-2)=2n^2-4n.
\]
Thus the displayed inequality holds for every positive integer \(n\).","claim":"Handles n=1 separately and, for n≥2, uses the potential-triple count and per-block bound to derive 14b(n) ≥ 2n²−4n.","depends_on":["n1","n2"],"scope":[],"goal_refs":[]}],"target_dependencies_after":["n1","n2"],"counterexample":null,"reason":"The replacement repairs the invalid use of T=2n(n−2) at n=1 by checking that case directly, while retaining the original covering argument for n≥2."}

{"problem": {"theorem": "I have an \(n \times n\) sheet of stamps, from which I've been asked to tear out blocks of three adjacent stamps in a single row or column. (I can only tear along the perforations separating adjacent stamps, and each block must come out of the sheet in one piece.) Let \(b(n)\) be the smallest number of blocks I can tear out and make it impossible to tear out any more blocks. Prove that there are real constants \(c\) and \(d\) such that

\[
\frac{1}{7} n^{2}-c n \leq b(n) \leq \frac{1}{5} n^{2}+d n
\]

for all \(n>0\).", "assumptions": [], "domain": "usamo", "explicit_subgoals": []}, "target": {"node_id": "n3", "version": 2}, "target_node": {"text": "Since in the final configuration every one of the \(T=2n(n-2)\) potential triples must be destroyed by at least one of the removed blocks, and since each block can destroy at most \(14\) triples, we get the inequality
\[
14\,b(n)\;\ge\;2\,n(n-2)\;=\;2n^2-4n,
\]", "claim": "Uses the potential-triple count and the per-block bound to derive 14b(n) ≥ 2n²−4n.", "scope": [], "depends_on": ["n1", "n2"], "goal_refs": []}, "closed_predecessors": [{"node_id": "n1", "version": 2, "claim": "Defines potential triples, correctly counts them for every positive integer n, including n=1, and states that every potential triple is hit in a blocked configuration.", "text": "Proof. We think of a final “blocked” configuration as the result of tearing out \(b(n)\) disjoint 3-stamp blocks, each lying in one row or one column, so that no further such block remains. Call any three consecutive positions in a row or column a “potential triple.” Each row contains \(\max\{n-2,0\}\) horizontal potential triples, and each column contains the same number of vertical potential triples. Hence
\[
H=V=n\max\{n-2,0\},\qquad T=2n\max\{n-2,0\}.
\]
In particular, these counts are zero when \(n=1\), and for \(n\ge2\) they equal \(H=V=n(n-2)\) and \(T=2n(n-2)\). Since the configuration is blocked, every potential triple must be hit, meaning that at least one of its stamps has been removed.", "scope": [], "depends_on": []}, {"node_id": "n2", "version": 2, "claim": "Bounds the number of potential triples hit by any single removed block by fourteen.", "text": "1.  Lower bound \(b(n)\ge \tfrac1{7}n^2-cn\).  
 
Fix any one of the \(b(n)\) removed blocks.  If it is a horizontal block occupying cells \((i,j),(i,j+1),(i,j+2)\), then it “hits’’ (i.e.\ destroys at least one cell of) at most
  •  all horizontal triples that include one of those three cells;  in a row of length \(n\), each interior cell lies in 3 horizontal triples and each end‐cell in 1 or 2, and one checks easily that the three consecutive cells \((i,j),(i,j+1),(i,j+2)\) together lie in at most 5 distinct horizontal triples;  
  •  all vertical triples that include one of those three cells;  each of the three removed stamps lies in at most 3 vertical triples, so altogether at most \(3\times3=9\) vertical triples.  
Hence that one horizontal block can destroy at most \(5+9=14\) of the \(T\) potential triples.  Likewise any vertical block destroys at most \(14\) potential triples.", "scope": [], "depends_on": ["n1"]}], "base_state_digest": "8afd8a09bf216d3c8abe4ca64bf15a212ae5022bb0234699eb8e00465003811f", "certificate": {"certificate_id": "c9e4b1bd76b3961204404c4419d6685de4793517389976ed36abdfcb5df6073a", "problem_digest": "4d1d82c46fdbd0fe41b8b6124f43970dbff707494470847d8da54f8f210a2f50", "target": {"node_id": "n3", "version": 2}, "graph_digest": "c66b70a84611faf25c9e26fb8a92ab806276d5a2fc3552d778724c16b1822ac1", "confirmation": "confirmed", "kind": "invalid", "failed_edge": "n1 -> n3", "quote": "Since in the final configuration every one of the \(T=2n(n-2)\) potential triples must be destroyed by at least one of the removed blocks", "reason": "The covering argument yields \(14b(n)\ge T=2n\max\{n-2,0\}\). Replacing this by \(2n(n-2)\) is justified only for \(n\ge2\). For \(n=1\), \(T=0\), not \(-2\). Although the displayed inequality happens to hold when \(n=1\), it requires a separate verification there."}, "limits": {"max_new_nodes_per_patch": 2, "max_total_node_edits": 6}}
